text.p: The Australian Securities Commission (ASC) said on Tuesday that it had assumed responsibility for the investigation into Bougainville Copper Ltd share trading earlier this year.
A spokeswoman for the regulator, Irene O'Brien, said the investigation was handed to the ASC by the Australian Stock Exchange (ASX) about three weeks ago.
O'Brien said the ASC was in the process of deciding how to proceed with the investigation but had not yet decided to send ASC officials overseas to interview any market participants.

She would not say if the ASC had identified brokers or principals involved in the heavy share dealings in February, which coincided with the announcement by the Papua New Guinea government that it planned to use mercenaries to rid Bougainville island of secessionist rebels.
"We are actually keeping that (the identity of buyers) fairly confidential right now," O'Brien said.
The island's giant Panguna copper mine was closed by the rebels in May 1989 and has not operated since then.
In early March, the PNG government offered to buy the controlling stake in the mine from Bougainville Copper's parent company, RTZ-CRA.

The ASX said last month that it was investigating unusually large turnover in Bougainville Copper in mid-February, when daily turnover rose to more than 460,000 -- 10 times higher than normal for the sleepy stock.
